events.title: Amiga 1000 released
events.summary: Commodore began selling the Amiga 1000 in July 1985 — a multimedia computer with custom graphics and sound chips ahead of its time.
events.about: The Amiga's Agnus and Denise chips delivered smooth scrolling, sprites, and stereo audio — demo scene coders and game developers pushed hardware tricks years before PC VGA caught up. AmigaOS multitasked with a message-passing kernel. The platform nurtured a generation of European game and multimedia developers before Commodore's decline.

narrative.whyChosen: The Amiga 1000 was the first consumer machine built for real-time graphics and sound.
narrative.whyImportant: It influenced game development, demo culture, and multimedia computing through the late 1980s.
narrative.problemSolved: PCs and Macs of the era could not deliver arcade-quality graphics and audio at consumer prices.
